title: Introduction, Pallet Town
question: How do I start the game after the initial cutscene?
answer: Press the A Button or Start on the title screen. This will lead you through a list of controls and a mission statement from the developers before Professor Oak appears.

title: Introduction, Pallet Town
question: How do I name my rival?
answer: You can choose a name for the rival from a list of preset names. If you prefer, you may also select a new name for him.

title: Introduction, Pallet Town
question: Who lives in the eastern house of Pallet Town?
answer: The eastern house is the home of your rival and his sister. This is one of the three main buildings located within the town.

title: Introduction, Pallet Town
question: What functions does the PC in the bedroom serve?
answer: The PC located in the corner of the room serves as your Mailbox. It also acts as your item storage, allowing you to deposit and withdraw items.

title: Introduction, Pallet Town
question: Where do I go to leave my bedroom?
answer: To go downstairs, you must step on the stairs located in the northeast corner of the room.

title: Introduction, Pallet Town
question: Why does Professor Oak stop you from entering the tall grass?
answer: He believes it is dangerous for you to venture out alone. You need a Pokémon of your own to defend yourself against wild Pokémon.

title: Introduction, Pallet Town
question: What happens to Charmander's typing in its final form?
answer: When Charmander reaches its final form, Charizard, it gains a secondary Flying type in addition to its Fire type.

title: Introduction, Pallet Town
question: What determines whether a battle is won or lost?
answer: A battle is decided when one side no longer has any Pokémon with the strength to continue. This occurs when all of the opponent's Pokémon have no remaining HP.

title: Introduction, Pallet Town
question: Where should I go after the battle with Blue is finished?
answer: Once Blue leaves, you should exit the laboratory. From there, head north to reach Route 1.

title: Route 1, Viridian City, Pallet Town (Revisited), Route 2 (West)
question: Where can I find the man who gives out free samples?
answer: You can find this man on the south side of the route. He is located near the signpost.

title: Route 1, Viridian City, Pallet Town (Revisited), Route 2 (West)
question: What services are provided at the Pokémon Center?
answer: The Pokémon Center acts as a hospital that restores your team to full health and removes any status ailments. Additionally, it provides a PC that allows Trainers to manage their item and Pokémon storage.

title: Route 1, Viridian City, Pallet Town (Revisited), Route 2 (West)
question: What items can be purchased at the Poké Mart?
answer: These stores provide a variety of items for the player. Specifically, you can buy different types of Poké Balls and Potions.

title: Route 1, Viridian City, Pallet Town (Revisited), Route 2 (West)
question: What must you do before you are allowed to make purchases at the shop?
answer: You must first take Oak's Parcel to Professor Oak. The shopkeeper will not allow you to buy items until this delivery is made.

title: Route 1, Viridian City, Pallet Town (Revisited), Route 2 (West)
question: Why is Professor Oak asking the player and Blue to gather information on Pokémon?
answer: It was Professor Oak's dream to gather information on all the Pokémon in the world himself. However, because of his advanced age, he must rely on you and Blue to complete this task.

title: Route 1, Viridian City, Pallet Town (Revisited), Route 2 (West)
question: Who gives the player the Town Map and where can they be found?
answer: The Town Map is given by Daisy. She can be found at your rival's house.

title: Route 1, Viridian City, Pallet Town (Revisited), Route 2 (West)
question: What can I do on Route 22 even though it cannot be fully explored yet?
answer: While you cannot fully explore Route 22 at this time, you can still use the area to hunt for new Pokémon. Additionally, you will encounter Blue shortly after entering the route.

title: Route 1, Viridian City, Pallet Town (Revisited), Route 2 (West)
question: What can I do if I have no Poké Balls and defeated Blue before catching any Pokémon?
answer: You can return to Pallet Town and speak with Professor Oak. He will provide you with 5 Poké Balls if you meet these conditions.

title: Viridian Forest, Pewter City, Pewter Gym
question: How do I find the Poké Ball in Viridian Forest?
answer: From the entrance of the forest, follow the trail toward the northwest. You will find the Poké Ball located within the tall grass in that area.

title: Viridian Forest, Pewter City, Pewter Gym
question: Which Bug Catchers will I encounter while navigating Viridian Forest?
answer: You will encounter Bug Catcher Rick on the east side of the forest. Later, you will pass Bug Catcher Doug and eventually defeat Bug Catcher Sammy near the northern edge.

title: Viridian Forest, Pewter City, Pewter Gym
question: What happens if I try to leave the city via the east exit?
answer: You will encounter a kid who is blocking the exit. This NPC will offer to escort you to the local Gym Leader, who is currently looking for challengers.

title: Viridian Forest, Pewter City, Pewter Gym
question: What are the type strengths and weaknesses of the Pokémon in the Pewter Gym?
answer: The gym specializes in Rock-type Pokémon, which are super effective against Bug, Fire, Flying, and Ice types. However, they are weak to Fighting, Grass, Ground, Steel, and Water moves. Because they are also partly Ground type, they are immune to Electric attacks.

title: Viridian Forest, Pewter City, Pewter Gym
question: What rewards do I receive after defeating Brock?
answer: Brock awards you the Boulder Badge and TM39, which contains the move Rock Tomb. These prizes are given to the player immediately after the battle.

title: Viridian Forest, Pewter City, Pewter Gym
question: How do the Running Shoes work in the game?
answer: The Running Shoes allow you to move faster than normal. To activate this speed boost, you must hold down the B Button while moving.

title: Route 3, Mt. Moon, Route 4
question: Is it worth buying the Magikarp from the shady man?
answer: Buying the fish allows you to obtain a strong Water-type Pokémon sooner than normal if you have the money. However, you can eventually catch a Magikarp for free if you have the correct fishing rod.

title: Route 3, Mt. Moon, Route 4
question: What items should I collect before heading east through the tunnel?
answer: You should collect TM09 (Bullet Seed) and the Parlyz Heal. These items are located to the west before you proceed eastward through the tunnel.

title: Route 3, Mt. Moon, Route 4
question: What should I do after battling the next two Trainers?
answer: After the battles, make sure to collect the Escape Rope, Rare Candy, and Potion. Then, head north and west before climbing down the second ladder.

title: Route 3, Mt. Moon, Route 4
question: How do I obtain the hidden Ether?
answer: To get the hidden Ether, you must inspect the large rock. This should be done before you return to 1F.

title: Route 3, Mt. Moon, Route 4
question: How do I find the fossils in the tunnel?
answer: Follow the winding tunnel in a clockwise direction toward the northwest. There, you will find Super Nerd Miguel, who has claimed the Dome Fossil and Helix Fossil as his own.

title: Route 3, Mt. Moon, Route 4
question: Which moves can be learned from the Black Belts on the western hill?
answer: The man on the left is able to teach Mega Punch to a compatible Pokémon. The man on the right can teach Mega Kick.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: What is required to get a Poliwhirl for trading?
answer: You must use a high-level fishing rod to find a Poliwhirl. This Pokémon is necessary if you wish to trade with the old man for his Jynx.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: Which Gym Badges are necessary to use field moves?
answer: You must obtain the first seven Gym Badges to unlock the use of field moves. This is one of the various effects explained by the man in the northwest house.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: How much does a Bicycle cost at the Bike Shop?
answer: A Bicycle costs $1,000,000. Because it is not possible to carry that much money, you cannot purchase one at this time.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: What are the strengths and weaknesses of Water-type Pokémon?
answer: Water-type moves are super effective when used against Rock-, Ground-, and Fire-type Pokémon. Conversely, Water-type Pokémon are weak to moves of the Grass and Electric types.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: Which specific moves are recommended for defeating Misty's Pokémon?
answer: To make quick work of her team, use Pikachu's ThunderShock. Alternatively, you can use Grass-type moves such as Bullet Seed and Vine Whip.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: What is the Fame Checker and how do you get it?
answer: The Fame Checker is a device used to record miscellaneous information about famous people, such as Gym Leaders. You receive this item as a gift from Blue after your battle near Route 24.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: What is the value of the Nugget found on Nugget Bridge?
answer: The Nugget is described as a bit of gold. It can be sold for a high price.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: What is the geography of Route 25?
answer: Route 25 consists of a path that winds through a forest. It eventually ends at a point that overlooks the sea.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: Where should you go to use the S.S. Ticket?
answer: You should travel south to Vermilion City. The luxury cruise ship is currently docked there.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: What is the effect of using Dig inside a cave?
answer: Using Dig while inside a cave will instantly return you to the entrance. This is a useful strategy when you are in a pinch and need to heal your Pokémon.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: How does a Pokémon gain experience while at the Day Care?
answer: A Pokémon left at the Day Care earns one experience point for every step you take. This makes it a useful method for raising a Pokémon like the Magikarp bought near Mt. Moon.

title: Cerulean City, Cerulean Gym, Route 24, Route 25, Route 5, Underground Path
question: Where can I find a girl willing to trade Nidoran?
answer: You can find a girl looking to trade in the north gate. She is offering either a Nidoran♀ or a Nidoran♂ depending on what you have.

title: Gameplay
question: How do I catch wild Pokémon in the game?
answer: You can find wild Pokémon in bodies of water, caves, and tall grass. To successfully catch these creatures, you will need to utilize various types of Poké Balls.

title: Gameplay
question: What triggers the reshuffling of reappearing items?
answer: Reappearing items are reshuffled and placed after the player has walked 1500 steps. The new items are then placed based on the group chosen for that specific area.

title: Gameplay
question: What content is added to the Pokédex once National Mode is active?
answer: Activating National Mode expands the Pokédex to include all Pokémon from the Johto and Hoenn regions.

title: Gameplay
question: How can I obtain one of the Legendary Beasts, and which one will I find?
answer: After defeating the Elite Four once, Entei, Raikou, or Suicune may appear randomly in the tall grass of the Kanto Region. The specific beast available is determined by the starter Pokémon you chose at the start of the game.

title: Gameplay
question: Has the typing for Magnemite changed?
answer: Yes, certain Pokémon have had their types changed. Magnemite is now an Electric/Steel type.

title: Gameplay
question: What updates have been made to Pokémon movesets?
answer: Movesets have been updated to include moves that were added in Generations II and III.

title: Gameplay
question: When can the Elite Four be re-challenged?
answer: The Elite Four are available to be challenged again after the initial completion. This allows the player to face them once more.

title: Raising Champions
question: What happens if there is a blank spot in the type matchup chart?
answer: A blank spot indicates that a move of that particular type is neither effective nor ineffective. It deals neutral damage to a Pokémon of the other type.

title: Raising Champions
question: What is the 'same-type attack bonus' (STAB)?
answer: STAB is a 50% power increase provided to attacks that are the same type as the Pokémon using them. For example, a Water-type Seel will be more effective using the Water-type move Surf than a non-Water-type like Nidoking.

title: Raising Champions
question: What is the function of the HP stat?
answer: The HP stat determines the amount of damage a Pokemon can sustain. Once this limit is reached, the Pokemon will faint.

title: Raising Champions
question: What are Individual Values (IVs) in the game?
answer: Individual Values are secret values that determine how a Pokémon's stats grow innately. Because these values differ for each individual Pokémon, two Pokémon of the same nature, level, and species may have slightly different stats.

title: Raising Champions
question: What is the relationship between Effort Values and stat increases at level 100?
answer: At level 100, roughly 4 EVs in a specific stat are equivalent to a +1 increase in that stat.

title: Raising Champions
question: How is the category of an attack determined in this game?
answer: The category of an attack is determined by its type. This determines whether a move utilizes the Attack or Sp. Atk stat.

title: Raising Champions
question: What is the difference between TMs and HMs when teaching moves?
answer: TMs are single-use items that teach a specific move based on compatibility. HMs can be used repeatedly to teach moves, but unlike TMs, they cannot be replaced by another move.

title: Raising Champions
question: What happens when a Pokémon tries to learn a new move but already knows four moves?
answer: One of the existing moves must be forgotten to make room for the new one. This process is necessary because a Pokémon can only know a maximum of four moves.

title: Raising Champions
question: How many abilities can an individual Pokémon have?
answer: An individual Pokémon can have one of up to two abilities. The specific abilities available are determined by the Pokémon's species.

title: Raising Champions
question: What occurs when a Pokémon affected by Bad poison switches out at the end of a battle?
answer: When a Pokémon with Bad poison switches out at the end of a battle, the condition transforms into regular poison. It can then be cured using the same methods used for regular poison.

title: Raising Champions
question: What are the penalties for a Pokémon suffering from Paralysis?
answer: Paralysis reduces a Pokémon's Speed stat to 25% and creates a 25% chance that the Pokémon will fail to use its move. This status is typically cured with a Parlyz Heal.

title: Raising Champions
question: What occurs when a Pokémon is Seeded?
answer: A Seeded Pokémon loses 1/8 of its max HP each turn. The amount of damage the Pokémon takes is then used to heal the opponent.

title: Raising Champions
question: When are status conditions such as stat reductions or confusion cured?
answer: These status conditions are cured once the battle ends. They will also be cured if the affected Pokémon is switched out.

title: Raising Champions
question: Under what conditions do some Pokémon evolve through trading?
answer: Certain Pokémon will only evolve after they have been traded to another player. This is the primary requirement for their evolution.

title: Raising Champions
question: What item can be used to permanently prevent a Pokémon from evolving?
answer: A Pokémon can hold an Everstone to stop it from evolving. This prevents evolution at all times, even if all necessary conditions for evolving have been met.

title: Raising Champions
question: Why is it important to have type variety on your team?
answer: Having too many Pokémon of a single type can be detrimental. This can lead to your team having a very poor matchup when facing certain types.

title: Catching Pokémon
question: How can I obtain Poké Balls in the game?
answer: You can acquire Poké Balls by purchasing them at the Poké Mart. Additionally, you may find Poké Balls as you travel on your way.

title: Catching Pokémon
question: How do I initiate a battle with a wild Pokémon?
answer: You can find wild Pokémon by entering the tall grass. Alternatively, you can use a "Pole" to fish or surf the seas to start a battle.

title: Catching Pokémon
question: How do I know if I have successfully captured a Pokémon?
answer: A successful capture occurs when the ball shakes three times, does not shake again, and is followed by a clicking lock.

title: Abilities
question: How many different Abilities can a single Pokémon species potentially have?
answer: A species may be capable of having one of two possible Abilities. For instance, a Diglett could have either Arena Trap or Sand Veil.

title: Pallet Town
question: What should I do before leaving my bedroom?
answer: You should withdraw the Potion from your computer. This is a precaution in case your rival puts up a good fight.

title: Pallet Town
question: How do I obtain my first Pokémon?
answer: First, step outside of town to search for Professor Oak, who will call out to warn you. Once you assemble with him and your rival, he will offer you a choice of three Pokémon.

title: Pallet Town
question: What happens when you try to exit town with your first Pokémon?
answer: Your rival will challenge you to a duel to test his mettle. You cannot refuse this battle before you are allowed to leave town.

title: Pallet Town
question: Who is Daisy and how does she feel about the player?
answer: Daisy is the sister of your lifelong rival. Unlike your rival, who carries a grudge and downplays you, Daisy is nice and thinks you are OK.

title: Route 1
question: What should I do if I encounter a battle that is too difficult for my Pokémon?
answer: If you find yourself in a battle that is too challenging, you should use the Run command. This will allow you to escape the fight.

title: Viridian City
question: What can I do at the Pokémon Center in Viridian City?
answer: You can visit the Pokémon Center to restore your Pokémon to full health. This is the first Pokémon Center you will encounter in the game.

title: Viridian City
question: What is preventing you from traveling north beyond Viridian City?
answer: Your path to the north is currently blocked by a sleeping man. He will not move, preventing further progress in that direction for the moment.

title: Viridian City
question: What items does the Professor give to the player and Blue?
answer: The Professor provides both the player and Blue with a Pokédex. Additionally, he gives each of them five Poké Balls.

title: Viridian City
question: Where can I find a hidden Potion in Viridian City?
answer: A Potion is hidden in the northwest corner of town. You can find it located behind a weird tree.

title: Viridian City
question: How can I get my Pokémon to learn Dream Eater?
answer: First, you must obtain the ability to Cut trees so you can speak with the man hiding beside the small lake. He can then teach your Pokémon Dream Eater, a Psychic technique.

title: Viridian City
question: What is the best strategy for catching wild Pokémon according to the guide?
answer: Wild Pokémon are easier to catch when they are in the yellow or red damage zones. Use a weak fighter to lower their health without knocking them out, or apply negative conditions like Sleep and Paralysis to increase your chances.

title: Route 22
question: What is a good alternative to Pidgey for a Flying-type Pokémon on this route?
answer: If you are patient, you can catch a Spearow. This Pokémon serves as a great alternative to Pidgey for players seeking a Flying-type for their party.

title: Route 22
question: How should I defeat the rival's Pidgey?
answer: The rival's Pidgey can be defeated easily using Thundershock. You can find a Pikachu to provide this move in Viridian Forest.

title: Route 2
question: Which Pokémon should I try to catch on Route 2, and which should I ignore?
answer: You should try to pick up a Pidgey or Rattata if you do not already have one. You can ignore Caterpie and Weedle for now, as they are more common inside the forest.

title: Viridian Forest
question: What should I do if I am struggling to defeat the trainers in the forest?
answer: If you are having trouble, it likely means your Pokémon are not strong enough and need to be leveled up. You should ensure most of your Pokémon are level 8 or above to be in good shape.

title: Viridian Forest
question: Why is it not recommended to capture wild Kakunas or Metapods?
answer: Wild and challenger-trained Kakunas and Metapods are unable to attack and can only use harden. Because they lack offensive moves, they are extremely difficult to train.

title: Viridian Forest
question: Where can I find a Poké Ball in the forest?
answer: You can find a Poké Ball located northwest of the entrance, marked as A on the map.

title: Pewter City
question: What can be found in Pewter City?
answer: Pewter City is the location of your first gym challenge. By completing this challenge, you will be able to earn your first badge.

title: Pewter City
question: Which Pokémon types are most effective against Brock and his Junior Trainer?
answer: Brock and his Junior Trainer use Ground and Rock type Pokémon. These types are weak to Water and Grass moves.

title: Pewter City
question: What are the benefits of obtaining the Boulder Badge?
answer: The Boulder Badge provides your Pokémon with a small power boost. Additionally, it allows you to use Flash outside of battle, provided you have already obtained HM05.

title: Pewter City
question: What information can be learned from the Museum's exhibits?
answer: The exhibits provide story details regarding fossil Pokémon and Mt. Moon. These exhibits are designed to help the player tie various plot points together.

title: Route 3
question: How do I obtain the Running Shoes and how are they used?
answer: Visit the entrance to Route 3 to meet Prof. Oak's Aide, who will give you the Running Shoes. Once you have them, you can run fast by pressing the B button.

title: Route 3
question: How can I identify hidden berries in the grass?
answer: Hidden berries are marked by a darkened oval on the grass. While they are visible, they can be difficult to notice until you know what they look like.

title: Mt. Moon
question: What should I do if I want to reach the end of Mt. Moon without fighting every trainer?
answer: Follow the path all the way to the end of the mountain. Once there, go down the very last ladder and continue following the path from that point.

title: Mt. Moon
question: What can be found in Mt. Moon in terms of Pokémon evolution items?
answer: Mt. Moon is the location where you will find your first Evolutionary Stones. Specifically, you can find Moon Stones here to evolve certain Pokémon.

title: Mt. Moon
question: What is the sequence of events to find the Escape Rope?
answer: Follow the south wall until you reach the corner. From the corner, head north to locate the Escape Rope.

title: Mt. Moon
question: Who are the trainers I will encounter while navigating toward the first ladder on the first floor?
answer: You will first face Bug Catcher Kent after moving left from the entrance. After heading east, you will encounter Lass Iris before reaching the first ladder.

title: Mt. Moon
question: What should I do while exploring this small section of the area?
answer: You should test your luck by checking the rocks for mushrooms. This is a good way to find items while navigating the section.

title: Mt. Moon
question: What should I do after dealing with the Team Rocket Grunt and finding the Star Piece?
answer: You should head back the way you came. From there, proceed to the first floor.

title: Mt. Moon
question: What is the sequence of events for navigating the path and dealing with Team Rocket?
answer: First, head north to collect a Revive, then return south to the stairs to battle a Team Rocket Grunt. Continue following the path until you encounter and defeat the final Team Rocket Grunt in the area.

title: Route 4
question: Where can I find a Persim Berry on Route 4?
answer: You can find a Persim Berry just outside the Pokémon Center. It is visibly hidden among the rocks in that area.

title: Route 4
question: Where can I find the Great Ball on Route 4?
answer: The Great Ball is a hidden item located on Route 4. You can find it to the left of the two Move Tutors at the top of the area.

title: Route 4
question: How do I navigate Route 4 after exiting Mt. Moon?
answer: Travel east, swerving north and south to avoid ledges. Eventually, the path turns north and then east again above a ledge that you cannot return over.

title: Cerulean City
question: How do I obtain a Powder Jar from the old man?
answer: Go to the house located to the right of the north west house and speak with the old man. He will give you a Powder Jar if you have already picked up a berry.

title: Cerulean City
question: What item do you receive after defeating your Rival near Bill's house?
answer: Once the battle with your Rival has ended, he will provide you with an item. This item is called a Fame Checker.

title: Cerulean City
question: What is required to obtain a Jynx from the old man?
answer: You must give the old man a Poliwhirl to receive a Jynx in return. The Jynx you receive will be at the same level as the Poliwhirl you trade.

title: Cerulean City
question: Which move should I use with Pikachu to beat Starmie, and when is it learned?
answer: You should use Thunderbolt, which is a powerful Electric-type move. Pikachu learns this move at level 26, and it can take Starmie down in one or two hits.

title: Cerulean City
question: Which Pokémon can be found on Routes 5 and 6 in LeafGreen versus FireRed?
answer: In LeafGreen, you can catch Bellsprout on Routes 5 and 6. In FireRed, you will find Oddish on those same routes, though it is less powerful than Bellsprout.

title: Route 24
question: Where can I find TM45 Attract on Route 24?
answer: After crossing the bridge, look for a platform located above the area where a trainer stands in the grass on the left. TM45 Attract is located on that platform.

title: Route 25
question: How do I return Bill to his human form?
answer: First, talk to the Clefairy at Bill's house and agree to help him. Then, go to the PC and press the button to make him emerge from the other side in human form.

title: Route 25
question: What should I do after speaking with Bill?
answer: Return to Cerulean City and defeat the Gym if you have not done so yet. Afterward, speak to the guard to proceed around the city down to Route 5.

title: Route 5
question: What happens when you leave Cerulean from the house where the guard was located?
answer: A Team Rocket Grunt will stop you to engage in a battle. You must defeat him as you attempt to leave the area.

title: Route 5
question: What should I do if the guards are blocking the way to Saffron City?
answer: You should head to the building located on the right. This building provides access to the Underground Path, which will lead you to Route 6.

title: Route 5
question: What are the chances of finding an item in the Underground Path?
answer: There is a 60% chance that you will find no items. There is a 30% chance of finding one of six uncommon items, and a 10% chance of finding a rare item.
